message:
feat(update): verify the manifest before believing a word of it

The rule is that nothing in a manifest counts until its signature checks out --
not the artifact hash, not even the version number. Rules like that survive a
refactor as comments and die as behaviour, so this one is a type instead:
parsed fields live behind VerifiedManifest, whose constructor is private and
whose only friend is load_manifest. Holding one is proof the signature passed,
and is_newer_than() hangs off it, so there is no path to a version comparison
that skips verification.

The ordering is also observable. A document that is both malformed and badly
signed must report SignatureInvalid -- a parse-first implementation would say
Malformed. The same garbage with a passing signature does report Malformed,
which is what shows the first case was decided by the signature and not by the
garbage.

ECDSA P-256 over SHA-256, raw r||s rather than DER, public key as raw X||Y.
All of it through BCrypt/CNG; nothing here implements cryptography. Every
failure returns the same false, because a caller cannot usefully tell a forgery
from an inability to check, and both mean the artifact is not known to be ours.

The manifest is line-oriented key=value text rather than JSON: the signature
covers exact bytes, and a format with no canonicalisation step has nothing to
disagree about between signer and verifier. Unknown keys are ignored so a newer
server cannot brick an older client; incompatible changes go through schema.

No release key is compiled in. trusted_public_key_hex() is empty, so the
default verifier rejects everything including the valid test signature -- and a
test asserts exactly that, so dropping in a placeholder that happens to verify
will fail the build rather than pass quietly. Real keys are a separate approval.

Test vectors were signed once with a throwaway P-256 key that was then
discarded; it is not stored and it is not a release key.
